limitations.note: The two-state rewrite keeps the second packed output unreachable instead of cycling through counts 0, 1, and 2 and emitting valid outputs on both the second and third accepted bytes.
The rewrite changes the already-working first output to use the second byte’s low nibble rather than preserving its high nibble.
The test expects the third accepted byte to produce no valid output, so it passes the rewrite while rejecting the required second packed word.
